deep.reconstruction:
This page has no formulas. It is a heavily corrected prose draft from the preparatory material for Riemann's 1851 Göttingen dissertation, 'Grundlagen für eine allgemeine Theorie der Functionen einer veränderlichen complexen Grösse'. The next page holds draft versions of the dissertation's opening definition: w is a function of z if dw/dz does not depend on dz. It also has a draft of the general mapping theorem, with constants counted against the order of connectivity. On the same sheet is an unrelated scratch derivation of the Fourier integral.

Content of this page, in order:

(a) Top lines, all struck out. These concern a surface T, its boundary, parallel lines, and a cross-cut (Querschnitt). They say the shape of the 'Schaaren' (families of curves) depends on the shape of the cross-cut.

(b) Main paragraph. Let T' be the surface obtained from T by cutting along a cross-cut. Traverse the boundary of T' from an arbitrary point in an arbitrary direction. One can then show that every part of the cross-cut is traversed twice, once along each bank. The pieces of T' are to be considered as long as they are not separated by pieces of the boundary of T, or by parts of the cross-cut traversed for the second time.
- Modern reading: cutting along an arc doubles it into two boundary arcs. This is the combinatorial fact behind Riemann's Art. 6 lemma. A cross-cut either joins two boundary components into one or splits one into two. Correspondingly it lowers the order of connectivity by one or disconnects the surface.

(c) Apart from this, the shape of the surface T' still depends on:
- (1) the windings of the cross-cuts;
- (2) the maximum and minimum of a certain quantity on the boundary of T.
The quantity is not named legibly. It is presumably a winding or turning count of the boundary, as in the dissertation's later counting of boundary windings against branch points. A point (3) is begun and left empty.

(d) Transitional sentences, several versions, mostly struck. These properties form the foundation for investigating the properties of a function. 'Before we undertake this investigation, some more general preliminary remarks are needed. S. 5.' And: 'First, some points belonging to a more general domain, not peculiar to our subject (cf. Art. 3).'
- This matches the dissertation's structure. The topological preliminaries on surfaces, cross-cuts and connectivity (Arts. 5–6) are inserted before the function-theoretic investigation.

No computation is performed. My interpretation (mine): the implicit claim is the effect of a single cross-cut. If T has connectivity order n and b boundary components, then T' has either order n−1 with b±1 components, or splits into two pieces.
errors: No mathematical errors can be assessed; the page is discursive draft prose with no derivations. Point (3) of the enumeration is left empty and the quantity in (2) is not clearly specified, so the argument is incomplete as drafted.

results.what: Traversal of the boundary of a surface cut along a cross-cut: each part of the cut is traversed twice, once along each bank. This underlies the effect of a cross-cut on boundary components and connectivity.
results.modern_name: Cutting a surface along an arc; change of connectivity/Euler characteristic under a cut (Riemann's Querschnitt lemma)

results.what: Plan of the dissertation: topological preliminaries on surfaces placed before the study of complex functions.
results.modern_name: Topology of Riemann surfaces as foundation of complex function theory

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft of passages in Riemann's published 1851 dissertation (cross-cuts, connectivity, preliminary remarks). Its content is well known and attributed to him. The page shows only drafting variants, with no new mathematics.

checkable.sympy: n, b = symbols('n b', integer=True); Eq((2 - 2*0 - b) - (2 - 2*0 - (b-1)) , -1)
checkable.asserts: Schematic bookkeeping: a cut joining two boundary components (b to b-1) on a planar domain changes the Euler characteristic 2-b by +1. Equivalently, it decreases Riemann's connectivity order by one. Illustrative only; not on the page.

transcription_corrections: Line 'von den Windungen ... von zweiblättrigen Querschnitten der Querschnitte': the reading 'zweiblättrigen' is doubtful. The image is better read as 'von den Windungen [-von den Rändern-] von ... Querschnitten', with 'der Querschnitte' as an interlinear insertion.
Item 2) reads roughly '2) von den [-...-] Maximum und Minimum dieser Grösse [-am Rande-] an der Begrenzung von T'. The second 'an der Begrenzung' is not struck as the transcription suggests.
Item '3).' stands alone, followed by the struck 'Wir werden'. The sentence 'welche ... bilden die Grundlage für die Untersuchung der Eigenschaften' belongs to a separate struck/revised passage.
The marginal '34' at right is the folio number, not part of the text.
Top-right interlinear insertion reads 'Die Begrenzung von T' and is an addition above 'Wenn man die Begrenzung von T von einem beliebigen Punkte aus'.
